g.text: A miniature study of structured reading notes
Original demonstration text · no real experiment is reported
Readers may confuse a claim with the evidence offered for it.
An argument map makes their relationship explicit.
We propose that structured notes make an argument easier to inspect.
This example uses a synthetic set of six short passages.
In the constructed set, four passages contain an explicit limitation.
The numbers describe the example, not observations from participants.
Figure 1. An argument map connects a claim to supporting passages
and separates evidence from the limits of an inference.
This illustration does not measure learning outcomes.
A controlled reader study would be needed to test that further claim.
